beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (railways, bridges, roads) and running a ready-mix concrete plant in Thane.

Contracts are won through a competitive bidding process: the client floats a tender, pre-bid meetings are held, the lowest bidder wins a letter of acceptance, and a performance guarantee is deposited.

Its major clients are government entities: Western Railway, Central Railway, MRVCL, MCGM, MMRDA, DFCCIL, and private firms. Western Railway alone contributed 57% of revenue in FY2018 and makes up 52% of the order book.
The company has a focused presence in Mumbai and Maharashtra, with a stated aim to consolidate its position in the state. It emphasises modern techniques like box pushing for bridge work.

business.heading: What the company does
business.purpose: Explain the two revenue segments, how contracts are won, key clients, and the order book.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations declined from ₹9,021.12 lakhs in FY2015 to ₹6,053.05 lakhs in FY2018, a drop of about 33% over four years.
Net profit after adjustments swung: it was ₹95.95 lakhs in FY2014, dropped to ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017, then surged to ₹314.66 lakhs in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) stood at ₹928.80 lakhs in FY2018, up from ₹676.19 lakhs in FY2017, but below the FY2015 level of ₹945.78 lakhs.
Short-term borrowings rose from ₹3,082.27 lakhs (FY2014) to ₹3,537.35 lakhs (FY2018), while long-term borrowings fell sharply from ₹672.72 lakhs to ₹133.09 lakhs over the same period.
The company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, a risk factor it acknowledges. Total assets grew from ₹7,062.34 lakhs (FY2014) to ₹8,232.15 lakhs (FY2018).
Key ratios: EPS was ₹1.31 (FY2016), ₹0.63 (FY2017), ₹12.59 (FY2018); RoNW was 4.14%, 1.97%, and 28.14% respectively.

beats.beat: Promoter Amit Bholanath Mishra holds 74,95,476 equity shares, representing 90.949% of the pre-issue capital.
Other directors hold 300 shares each. Key management includes CFO Anchal Pachori (CA) and CS Mohit Soni (ACS).
Related-party transactions: loans from KMP/ directors of ₹68.4 lakhs, director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables to related parties of ₹324.3 lakhs as of FY2018.

The filing notes that two companies promoted by Mr. Mishra (Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited) were struck off by the ROC in 2016 for non-operation. The company has also issued shares in the past 12 months at a price that may be lower than the issue price.

beats.beat: The Indian infrastructure sector contributes about 8% to GDP and is highly fragmented with intense competition from organised and unorganised players.

Growth drivers include government flagship programmes (Smart Cities, AMRUT, Make in India), eased FDI norms, and rising urbanisation. The 12th Five-Year Plan targeted infrastructure spending at 9% of GDP.
The filing notes headwinds: slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches, and changes in government policies that could affect profitability.

It is raising ₹[●] crore through a fresh issue of 44.28 lakh equity shares on the SME Board, with proceeds earmarked primarily for working capital.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each; there is no offer for sale. The issue price is to be determined.
Proceeds of ₹1,130 lakhs are allocated to meet working capital requirements; a residual amount will go towards general corporate purposes.
The lead manager is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited; the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.

offer.heading: Offer structure and use of proceeds
offer.purpose: Detail the fresh issue, objects, and lead manager.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: 57% of FY2018 revenue came from Indian Railways (mainly Western Railway). Loss of this customer would cause a significant revenue drop.
Negative cash flows and working capital strain: the company reports negative cash flows in recent years and has ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans repayable on demand, which could pressure liquidity.
Dependence on government contract bidding: revenues depend on winning bids from government departments. Non-acceptance or lower bid values can materially affect performance.

Promoter-related red flags: two struck-off companies previously promoted by the promoter raise governance concerns, and equity shares were issued in the last 12 months at a price possibly below the IPO price.

No independent appraisal: the company has not appointed any independent agency to appraise the use of proceeds, and no monitoring agency has been appointed, so fund deployment is solely at management discretion.
